blocks.text: **Debate writing (vaadopavaadam)** presents a **reasoned argument for or against a proposition** on a current or editorial issue in Telugu — with a clear stance, supporting points, rebuttal of the opposing view, and a persuasive conclusion.

rows: Greeting + state the topic and your stance (for/against).
Anticipate and counter the opposing view.
Assertive but respectful; logical, not emotional.

items: Take a **clear stance** and stick to it throughout.
Support each point with **evidence or example**.
**Address the counter-view** and refute it.
Stay **logical, respectful and persuasive**.

mainsAngles: Practise for/against debates on current and editorial issues with clear stance and rebuttal.
Support arguments with evidence and maintain a respectful, persuasive tone.

glossary.definition: The counter to an opposing argument in a debate.

blocks.text: **Application writing (vinnapam / arji)** is a formal request in Telugu — for leave, a job, a certificate, or redressal — following the **formal-letter format** with a polite, precise statement of the request and its grounds.

items: Follow the **formal-letter format**; be concise and polite.
State the **request clearly** and give a brief justification.
Include necessary details (dates, references).
Keep grammar and spelling correct.

mainsAngles: Practise leave/job/certificate applications in correct formal Telugu format.
State the request and its grounds clearly and politely.

glossary.definition: A formal application or request in Telugu.
A one-line statement of the application's purpose.

blocks.text: A Telugu **report (nivedika)** gives a factual, structured account of an **event, function or survey** in the **past tense and objective third person**, with a clear title, sequential body and a concluding outcome.

rows: Sequence of events / findings in logical order.
Past tense, third person, objective, factual Telugu.

items: Write in the **past tense, third person, objective** voice.
Lead with the **essentials (what/when/where/who)**.
Keep chronological or thematic order; stay factual.
For a **survey report**, present findings clearly with figures.

mainsAngles: Practise event/function/survey reports in objective, past-tense Telugu.
Present findings and outcomes clearly and factually.

glossary.definition: Impersonal, factual writing without personal opinion.

blocks.text: **Dialogue writing (samvadam)** presents a **natural conversation between two or more people** in Telugu on a given situation or theme — testing colloquial fluency, turn-taking and the ability to convey ideas through exchange.

rows: The dialogue should develop the theme/reach a point.
Speaker name : dialogue line (each on a new line).

items: Keep exchanges **natural and colloquial**, not bookish.
Ensure **clear turn-taking** with speaker labels.
Let the dialogue **progress** toward a point or resolution.
Match **tone/register** to the speakers and situation.

mainsAngles: Practise natural two-person Telugu dialogues on given situations.
Develop the theme through realistic, well-turned exchanges.

glossary.definition: A dialogue or conversation in Telugu.
The level of formality matched to the speakers and situation.

blocks.text: **Translation from English to Telugu (anuvadam)** tests conveying **meaning faithfully and idiomatically** in Telugu — capturing sense, tone and register rather than translating word-for-word, in grammatically correct Telugu.

rows: Translate the meaning, not literally word-by-word.
Use idiomatic Telugu; recast to fit Telugu syntax.
Match the formality/tone of the source.
Use standard Telugu equivalents or explain.

items: Read the whole passage to grasp **overall sense** first.
Translate **meaning and tone**, recasting into natural Telugu.
Use **standard Telugu terms** for technical/administrative words.
Keep **fidelity** and correct grammar; proofread.

mainsAngles: Practise sense-for-sense English-to-Telugu translation in natural idiom.
Preserve tone, register and meaning with correct Telugu grammar.

glossary.definition: Translating meaning and effect rather than word-for-word.

blocks.text: Telugu **grammar (vyakaranam)** underlies correct writing — the rules of **sandhi (junction), samasam (compounds), vibhakti (case), and alankaram/chandas (figures & prosody)**. Accuracy in these is essential across all writing tasks and directly tested.

rows: Rules for the junction/combination of sounds/words.
Compound words formed by joining words.

items: Master the common **sandhi** and **samasam** types with examples.
Know the **vibhaktis (cases)** and their correct usage.
Learn key **alankaras** (upama, rupaka, etc.) with examples.
Apply grammar correctly in **all writing tasks**, not just grammar questions.

mainsAngles: Master sandhi, samasam, vibhakti, alankaram and chandas with examples.
Apply Telugu grammar accurately across all composition tasks.

glossary.definition: The rules governing the combination/junction of sounds and words in Telugu.
Case markers/postpositions showing a word's grammatical function.
A figure of speech in Telugu poetics (word or meaning based).
